presentation_rule: Forecast, then assumptions of at most 150 words, then downloads. Supporting research belongs in downloads. Presentation changes do not refresh model dates or estimates.

1723.caption: ¥ billion, except EPS and margins · G = company guidance; E = JII estimate
1723.forecast_notes: FY3/27 is company guidance. FY3/28 sales and OP match the company’s medium-term targets; its net income and EPS are JII calculations. FY3/29–30 are JII estimates.
bullets: Sales: ¥51.5bn in FY3/27, then ¥52bn, ¥54.5bn and ¥57bn. FY3/28 uses the company’s medium-term sales target; subsequent growth is JII’s assumption.

Margins: 24.27%, 25.00%, 24.80% and 24.60%. FY3/28 OP matches the company’s ¥13bn target. Later margins are JII estimates; the model assumes easing without separately quantifying its underlying cost or pricing changes.

EPS: net income remains 69.6% of OP, using the FY3/27 guidance ratio. Weighted shares stay at 63.741m, so future buybacks do not contribute to EPS growth. Delivery, pricing or costs differing from these sales and margin assumptions would change the forecast.
1723.download_note: The dated comparison ZIP also contains an older Dai-Dan forecast; use the current Dai-Dan page below.

1969.caption: ¥ billion, except EPS and margins · G = company guidance; E = JII estimate
1969.forecast_notes: FY3/27 is company guidance; FY3/28–30 are JII estimates.
bullets: Sales: ¥440bn in FY3/27, then ¥463bn, ¥487bn and ¥512bn. The starting year is company guidance; later sales growth of roughly 5% annually is JII’s assumption.

Margins: OP margin rises from 11.36% to 11.50%, 11.70% and 11.80%. This improvement is a JII estimate; the model does not separately quantify annual pricing, staffing and cost changes. Failure to achieve it would reduce forecast EPS.

EPS: net income stays at 80% of OP, matching the FY3/27 guidance ratio. Weighted shares remain 130.877m. EPS growth therefore comes from the assumed sales growth and margin improvement, with no contribution from future buybacks.
1969.download_note: The dated comparison ZIP also contains an older Dai-Dan forecast; use the current Dai-Dan page below.

1980.caption: JII base-case estimates in every year · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
1980.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate. FY3/27 OP of ¥48.10bn compares with company guidance of ¥42.00bn. Recurring EPS excludes identified exceptional gains and differs from reported or company-guided EPS.
bullets: Profit retention: the base carries forward the full observed improvement in like-for-like half-year cash gross margin, consistent with improved bidding and execution. This is the most important judgment: retaining half would reduce FY3/30 EPS from ¥319 to about ¥297.
Delivery: staffing grows 5.03% annually, anchored to the latest full-year group headcount increase; productivity adds 1% from FY3/28. These are JII capacity proxies, not disclosed physical output.
Pricing and costs: new bids and nonlabor inputs rise 4% annually; pay rises 5%, informed by the disclosed three-year base-pay increase. Existing bids retain their original prices.
Margins and EPS: overhead grows faster than sales, easing OP margin from 17.5% to 17.0%. The model uses a 31.01% normalized tax rate, separate minority claims and no unexecuted buybacks.

5842.caption: JII base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS · December year ends
5842.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY12/26 combines actual H1 and estimated H2. ¹ Fee-only EPS excludes carry and investment income. ² Total EPS includes conditional carry and investment returns. ³ FY12/26 investment calls cover H2 only. Cash/debt are year-end balances. ⁴ Cash precedes unallocated disposal tax; the stress deducts the full ¥11.2bn opening deferred-tax balance and remaining GP calls.
bullets: Fees: a 1.95% management-fee proxy applies to fund commitments and declining older-fund fee bases. Harvesting-fund fee exposure falls from ¥86bn to ¥26bn by 2029; fixed costs rise 7.12% annually, initially squeezing fee earnings.
Fundraising: an unannounced ¥250bn successor fund is assumed to close during 2029, contributing half-year fees. Without it, FY12/29 fee-only EPS falls from ¥60.12 to ¥16.33.
Carry: assumed additional realizations of ¥1bn in H2 2026, then ¥4bn/¥6bn/¥7bn, draw on the disclosed ¥22bn unrealized pool. Timing is uncertain; carry is separate from recurring fees.

Cash and EPS: principal investment marks are flat; GP calls and investment returns drive cash. Tax is 30.6%, basic shares 34.067m, with separate minority claims and no buybacks. Cash is not wholly available for distribution.

6184.caption: JII base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
6184.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY1/27 combines actual H1 and estimated H2. Basic EPS retains known H1 exceptional items; none recur in future estimates. ¹ Cash flows cover full fiscal years. Operating FCF deducts cash capex and long-term prepaid investment.
bullets: Growth: seven business lines are forecast separately. FY1/28–30 care revenue growth slows from 30% to 20%, municipal services from 23% to 18%, funerals from 16% to 12%, and graves from 9% to 7%. H1 referrals, sales and municipal partnerships anchor these JII estimates.

Margins: advertising follows noninsurance sales; wages rise 3%, with hiring responding to the care/municipal mix. Other costs rise by 2% inflation plus 60% of incremental activity growth. Costs grow more slowly than revenue, lifting margins.
Investment: annual cash capex rises from ¥0.60bn to ¥0.75bn; software spending feeds depreciation rather than becoming a free earnings benefit.
EPS: future tax is 31.5% before nondeductible goodwill. Separate minority claims and 41.195m basic shares are retained; no new acquisition or buyback is assumed.

6617.caption: JII base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
6617.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY3/27 combines actual H1 and estimated H2. Recurring EPS excludes identified one-offs. ¹ Cash flows cover full fiscal years; operating FCF deducts cash capex and excludes property proceeds. Estimates retain an after-rent basis; the future lease-accounting effect is unquantified.
bullets: Deliveries: Power orders and real-workload capacity grow 4.5% annually after FY3/27. Backlog conversion is constrained by engineering, testing and acceptance. Metering order growth slows to 3%/2%/1% as the replacement cycle matures; these are JII financial proxies.

Margins: Power/Metering new-order prices rise 2%/1.5%, versus 1.5% input inflation. Old contracts keep vintage prices. Fixed costs rise about 3%; corporate spending and depreciation increase. Slower metering growth and these costs weigh on later OP.
Investment and cash: capex is ¥6.5bn/¥7.5bn/¥7.0bn/¥6.5bn. The estimated ¥8.188bn remaining property receipt in FY3/28 is outside operating FCF; final consideration is undisclosed.
EPS: tax is 31.5%; weighted shares fall from 15.583m to 15.400m, then stay flat. No additional buyback is assumed.

9037.caption: JII base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins · Pre-adoption lease basis
9037.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY3/27 earnings combine actual H1 and estimated H2. ¹ FY3/27 cash capex, CFO and FCF cover H2 only; later years are full fiscal years. FCF deducts cash capex and finance-lease principal, before dividends, acquisitions and bank repayments. Cash/debt are year-end balances; available cash excludes an assumed time-deposit reserve.
bullets: Revenue: existing center and trucking activity is flat. Center wins add 4.5% of prior-year sales, against 1% churn. Center/trucking prices rise 2%/2.2% annually, anchored to customer starts and reported segment trends.

Margins: wages rise 3.5% and other variable inputs 1.5%, offset by assumed center/truck productivity gains of 1.4%/1.7%. Pricing, new work and productivity lift OP; these are JII estimates rather than disclosed unit economics.
Investment and funding: FY3/28–30 capex is ¥13.30bn/¥11.62bn/¥12.24bn, including named projects. Annual bank repayments are ¥3.5bn; funding depends on preserving a ¥15bn cash reserve.

EPS: tax is 33.5%, with separate subsidiary minority claims and 74.050m later-year basic shares. No new acquisition or buyback is assumed. Operating rents remain expensed; the new lease standard’s statutory effect is unquantified.

9211.caption: JII conditional base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
9211.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY12/26 earnings combine actual H1 and estimated H2. ¹ Recurring earnings exclude liability-revaluation income and impairment; EPS retains interest, tax and minority claims. ² FY12/26 seller payments cover H2 only; later years are full years. Cash/debt are year-end balances.
bullets: Growth: H2 activity rises 6%, then 8%/6.5%/5% annually. Existing acquisitions are annualized; no new M&A is assumed.
Margins: price/mix improves 1.5%, versus 2.5% variable-input inflation and 5.5% fixed-cost growth. Slower activity growth leaves less cost absorption, easing later margins.

Seller obligations: puts settle 0%/20%/30%/50% of the original covered pool; earnouts settle 10%/25%/30%/35%. Payment amounts track assumed acquired-company earnings. The ¥750m fixed AI ONE price is treated as additional. Actual exercise terms and ownership mapping remain uncertain.

Funding and EPS: seller payments reduce cash while settling covered minority claims increases parent earnings. Refinancing is uncommitted and limited to repayments; additional need triggers discounted equity issuance. Tax is 30%; no future liability-revaluation gains are included. These funding and payment assumptions make the forecast particularly uncertain.
